# autoseed (Go)

> Reads a GORM model via schema.Parse, derives foreign-key insertion order (stable topological
> sort), and resolves nullable cycles in two passes, so nothing about entities, ordering or
> relationships needs declaring by hand. Status: in development. Today the library reads a model
> and reports the plan (gormseed.Explain); it does not yet generate or write data.

Unlike every other Go seeder, nothing will be declared by hand once value generation ships — no
YAML fixtures, no hand-written Seed() loops, no files numbered 01_, 02_ to get foreign-key order
right. The model is the specification.

Sibling project: EFCore.AutoSeed (same author, same design, .NET).

- Module: `github.com/danellalc/autoseed`
- Adapters: `autoseed/gormseed` (GORM, implemented), `autoseed/entseed` (ent, planned)
- Databases (once Seed exists): PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite
- License: MIT
- Status: in development — read "Implemented today" vs "Planned" below before generating code

## Install

```bash
go get github.com/danellalc/autoseed
```

## Implemented today

```go
import "github.com/danellalc/autoseed/gormseed"

models := []any{&Customer{}, &Order{}, &OrderItem{}}

// Reads the model, derives insertion order, resolves nullable cycles. Writes nothing.
plan, err := gormseed.Explain(db, models)
fmt.Println(plan.Report())
```

`db` may be `nil`, or not yet connected to a real database — reading a model is pure reflection,
no connection needed. `models` is the exhaustive set of GORM structs to include: a `*gorm.DB`
keeps no registry of every struct it has ever used, unlike an EF Core `DbContext`, so the list is
stated explicitly on every call.

The `autoseed/inference` package (~15 value-generation rules, gofakeit-backed) is built and
tested but not yet wired to any public `gormseed` function — nothing calls it from `Explain` or
from a `Seed` that doesn't exist yet. One rule runs unconditionally, with no opt-in: any string
field named `Cpf` or `Cnpj` (case-insensitive suffix, any project) generates a Brazilian document
number with a valid check digit. This is not locale-gated — there is no locale mechanism yet — so
a non-Brazilian project with a coincidentally matching field name gets Brazilian-format data.

## Planned, not implemented yet

These identifiers do not exist in the module. Do not generate calls to them.

```go
err := gormseed.Seed(db, models, autoseed.WithSeed(42), autoseed.WithScale(1_000))
err := gormseed.SeedCoverage(db, models)
```

Planned functional options, none implemented yet: `WithSeed(uint64)`, `WithScale(int)`,
`WithLocale("pt_BR")`, `WithNilRate(0.2)`.

## Guarantees (today's scope: reading and Explain)

- Every Reference in a resolved Plan targets an entity present in `models`, or Explain returns
  `autoseed.ErrUnknownReference` naming what is missing.
- Same model, same Explain output, across runs and machines — map iteration never affects it.
- Embedded structs are read as columns, never as their own entity.
- An unsatisfiable model (a required foreign key cycle) returns `autoseed.ErrUnsatisfiableCycle`
  naming the real cycle, rather than a database throwing a constraint violation later.
- Unsupported constructs (polymorphic associations, for now) are skipped BY NAME in the Explain
  report, never silently misread.

Guarantees about generated data — every foreign key pointing at a real row, soft-deleted rows in
realistic proportion, deterministic generated values for a given seed — describe the design and
apply once `Seed` ships. They are not true of any code path today.

## Common mistakes when using this library

- Do not generate a call to `gormseed.Seed` or `gormseed.SeedCoverage` — neither exists yet.
  `gormseed.Explain` is the one thing that runs today.
- Do not omit a related model from `models` — `Explain` returns `ErrUnknownReference` naming
  what's missing, rather than a partial or guessed plan.
- Do not order entities manually. Order is derived from the model's foreign keys.
- Polymorphic associations are read but not generated; they appear as skipped in the Explain
  report, never as a reference.

## Not supported

- ORMs other than GORM (ent is planned; others on demand with traction).
- Databases other than PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, once `Seed` exists.
- Production data anonymisation. No cloud, no service.
